verdictStatement: My v1 SHOULD-FIX is repaired exactly as specified, and the repair is the honest shape rather than the convenient one: the moved COORDINATOR-DECISIONS pin is not silently re-pinned but labelled INHERITED-V1-AUTHORING-PIN with measuredAtV1Authoring, its role narrowed to the three named properties, and the live digest segregated at reMeasurementAtV2. The blanket sentence that made the v1 defect sharp — 'Measured in this authoring session. The bound is the claim' — is replaced by a precise split naming which five pins remain v1 measurements, and I re-measured all five: every one still reproduces. Every claim in the new remeasurement block is checkable and checks out, including the two I expected to be loose: measuredAtHead 36949e3 is the current HEAD exactly, and file08Unchanged matches live file 08. The three named COORD properties are re-verified in the artifact and I confirmed each independently at live bytes. Nothing substantive moved: eighteen blocks including all eight properties, the carried file-04 text, the register row and every dependency are byte-identical to v1, so the property, encoding, D9, lock-collapse and producibility attacks all still fail — the token 'producib' appears zero times. advisories.title: /date changed but is not on the closed roster, and the roster's 'succession metadata' escape category is undefined
advisories.detail: v1 is stamped 2026-08-14 and v2 is stamped 2026-08-15. basedOn.method enumerates an eleven-path Closed roster that includes /artifact and /version but not /date, and closes with 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v1.' That sentence reserves an unrostered succession-metadata category which this artifact never enumerates, so whether /date qualifies is left to the reader. A full recursive diff finds twelve changed paths; eleven are rostered and /date is the twelfth.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The closure sentence is not falsified under any fair reading: an authoring-date stamp is the canonical succession-metadata field, and the change is not merely benign but obligatory — a v2 authored on the 15th must not keep claiming the 14th. The field carries no authority, no measurement, and no claim about any other artifact, so a coordinator who bounded their re-read by the roster would miss nothing of consequence. I record it because the roster does list /artifact and /version, which makes the omission of the third identity field look like an oversight rather than a deliberate carve-out.
advisories.whyThisIsNotGradedAsIWouldGradeAnUnroste: I have graded an unrostered path as SHOULD-FIX elsewhere in this corpus when the field was /authorityClaim — the sentence stating what an artifact claims authority to do, which a roster-bounded re-read would skip at real cost. The distinction here is stakes, not principle: /date is inert. Recording the reasoning so the difference does not read as inconsistency.
advisories.suggestedFix: Either add /date to the roster alongside /artifact and /version, or enumerate the succession-metadata set once — /artifact, /version, /date, /basedOn, /appliesFindingsOf, /honestyRepairsFromV1 — so the escape category stops being undefined.

coordinatorNote: This is a clean, narrowly-scoped successor. The v1 finding was that the artifact bound itself with 'the bound is the claim' while one of six bounds had gone stale through ordinary lane progress; v2 fixes it the honest way, keeping the stale value visible and labelled rather than quietly refreshing it, and replacing the blanket sentence with a split that is true. I checked the new remeasurement block against live bytes rather than reading it, including the HEAD commit and the negative claim about file 08, and all of it holds. The eight file-04 properties and every other substantive block are byte-identical, so nothing regressed while the pin was being repaired. The single advisory is that the authoring date stamp moved without being named on a roster that does list /artifact and /version; the field is inert and the roster's undefined 'succession metadata' category fairly covers it, which is why it does not withhold acceptance — I have set out in the finding why I grade this differently from an unrostered authority-bearing field. DR-107 stays at PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, no encoding is chosen, no loss code is invented, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
